channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan Delegation Attends Belgrade Summit on Non-Aligned Movement's 65th Anniversary
item.description: Uzbekistan's delegation, led by Senate First Deputy Speaker Sodik Safoev, participated in a high-level meeting in Belgrade commemorating the 65th anniversary of the Non-Aligned Movement. Safoev discussed Uzbekistan's upcoming 2027-2030 chairmanship and priorities, including peace, security, economy, climate change, and youth issues.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea explore pharmaceutical cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan's Agency for the Development of the Medical and Pharmaceutical Industry met with leading South Korean pharmaceutical clusters, KBIO Health and K-MEDI hub. Discussions focused on cluster-to-cluster cooperation, R&D infrastructure, training, and technology transfer, particularly for mRNA vaccines and oncology.

item.title: Uzbek President discusses strengthening strategic partnership with US Senator
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with US Senator Steve Daines to discuss strengthening the strategic partnership between Uzbekistan and the United States. They reviewed bilateral cooperation, economic and investment ties, and regional cooperation formats like 'C5+1'.

item.title: Violations Found in Kyrgyz River's Water Protection Zone in Talas Region
item.description: Violations of land and water legislation were discovered in the water protection zone of the Kayyndy River in Kyrgyzstan's Talas region. The Ministry of Agriculture reported that houses were built near the water, and a road construction damaged the soil cover. Fines were imposed, and violations must be rectified within 30 days.

item.title: Putin Sees Possibility of Reaching Agreement to End Ukraine War
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin stated there is a possibility of reaching an agreement to end the war in Ukraine. He described reports of attacks on civilian merchant ships and civilian aircraft by Ukraine as "acts of state terrorism."

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans to Build Vaccine Production Plant for Animal Diseases
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to construct a plant for producing biological preparations, including vaccines against viral and bacterial diseases, and foot-and-mouth disease. The initiative aims to strengthen veterinary security and establish domestic vaccine production.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Discusses Strengthening Strategic Partnership with US Senator
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev held discussions with a US Senator regarding the further strengthening of the strategic partnership between Uzbekistan and the United States. They also reviewed ways to develop inter-parliamentary cooperation.

item.title: Issyk-Kul Residents Establish Micro-Reserve for Rare Birds
item.description: A Bird Fest 2026 was held in the village of Yntymak, Kyrgyzstan, to conserve birds and biodiversity in the Tyup Bay. Residents, schoolchildren, and scientists participated in creating a public micro-reserve on territory where up to 280 bird species have been recorded, including nine endangered ones.

item.title: New Western Bus Station in Bishkek Set to Open in September
item.description: The new Western Bus Station in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, is scheduled to open in September, with 95 percent of construction completed. The facility will include shops, waiting areas, and parking, covering 30,000 square meters on a 16-hectare site. The old station closed in October 2024.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva meets with Emir of Qatar to discuss expanding relations
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva met with the Emir of Qatar. During the meeting, discussions focused on further expanding mutual relations and advancing new joint initiatives. This meeting signifies efforts to strengthen bilateral ties between the two nations.

item.title: Flights from Bishkek to Moscow and Novosibirsk delayed
item.description: Flights by Russian airlines Aeroflot and S7 Airlines from Bishkek to Moscow and Novosibirsk were delayed on September 3. Kyrgyzstan Airports stated the delays but did not provide reasons. Ukrainian President Zelensky previously warned of dangers in Russian airspace.

item.title: Uzbekistan is a driving force in the Organization of Turkic States, says Secretary General
item.description: Kubanychbek Omuraliev, Secretary General of the Organization of Turkic States, congratulated Uzbekistan on its 35th Independence Day. He highlighted Uzbekistan's significant contributions to the Turkic world's unity through initiatives in transport, trade, digital transformation, education, culture, and regional dialogue. Omuraliev noted Uzbekistan's reforms under President Shavkat Mirziyoyev have strengthened its international standing.

item.title: UN Women's Fund needs over $150 million to combat violence against women
item.description: The UN Trust Fund in Support of Actions to Eliminate Violence against Women and Girls has mobilized over $250 million and supported over 700 initiatives globally in 30 years. However, demand for support significantly exceeds its capacity, with over $2 billion in requests for 2025 alone. UN Secretary-General António Guterres urged renewed investment in women's organizations.

item.title: Road collapse in Tashkent injures one person; pipeline suspected cause
item.description: A road collapse in Tashkent injured one person while cars were moving. Veolia Energy, "Tashkent City Water Supply" JSC, and "Hududgaz Poytaxt" gas supply branch commented on reports that an underground pipeline caused the incident.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Rights group reports continued persecution of government critics
item.description: The International Partnership for Human Rights (IPHR) has released a report on civil space and freedom of expression in Kyrgyzstan. The report concludes that persecution of government critics continues despite recent dismissals.

item.title: Russia: Kyrgyzstan-born teenager sentenced to seven years for gas station arson
item.description: A 15-year-old girl, whose parents are from Kyrgyzstan, has been sentenced to seven years in a juvenile colony in Russia for setting fire to a gas station. She was found guilty of terrorism causing significant property damage.

item.title: Uzbekistan's service exports, driven by tourism, become largest income source
item.description: Uzbekistan's foreign trade turnover reached $49.5 billion in Jan-Jul, an 8.1% increase. Exports fell 3.6% to $19.93 billion, while imports rose 17.8% to $29.6 billion. Service exports, boosted by tourism, have become the largest source of income, despite a 63.1% drop in gold exports.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Secures Second Kok-Boru Victory at World Nomad Games
item.description: The Kyrgyzstan national team achieved its second consecutive victory in the kok-boru tournament at the 6th World Nomad Games, defeating Uzbekistan 16-11. Kyrgyzstan currently leads its group with six points.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev congratulates Mirziyoyev on Uzbekistan's 35th Independence Day at SCO Summit
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev congratulated Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov on their countries' 35th independence anniversaries during the SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan. Tokayev thanked Kyrgyzstan for its hospitality and praised the SCO's growth into a major international organization over 25 years, emphasizing mutual trust and respect for sovereignty.

item.title: Road collapses on Glinka Street in Tashkent, one injured
item.description: A section of asphalt collapsed on Glinka Street in Tashkent's Yakkasaroy district, creating a crack. Social media suggests an underground pipe explosion caused the incident. Several cars were damaged, and one person sustained minor injuries, receiving prompt medical attention. Traffic on Glinka Street is temporarily suspended.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Security Council emphasizes maintaining high security for World Nomad Games
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Security Council Secretary Adilet Orozbekov stated that major international events held recently concluded without incident, crediting joint efforts of security forces. He stressed the need to maintain heightened security measures throughout the VI World Nomad Games in Cholpon-Ata. Additional instructions were given to state bodies and local authorities.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Significantly Increased Fines for Aviation Violations
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Civil Aviation Agency is proposing substantial increases to fines for aviation-related offenses. The draft legislation, now open for public discussion, could see penalties rise severalfold, with some fines increasing by over 30 times. For instance, fines for airspace violations could jump from 7,500 to 100,000 som for individuals and from 23,000 to 500,000 som for legal entities.

item.title: Climate Change to Disproportionately Affect Vulnerable Groups in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Climate change in Kyrgyzstan is predicted to most severely impact vulnerable populations, including women, children, the elderly, people with disabilities, and low-income families. The National Adaptation Plan highlights that over 57% of the population relies on agriculture, making them susceptible to droughts and water shortages. Women, often responsible for household water and food, face increased burdens as resources decline.

item.title: Four Uzbek citizens arrested in South Korea for financing terrorism
item.description: Four Uzbek citizens have been arrested in South Korea on suspicion of financing a terrorist group in Syria. One individual allegedly sent $4,600 in cryptocurrency to the "Katiba at-Tavhid val-Jihod" terrorist organization. He is also suspected of purchasing vehicles and excavators for the group.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's National Bank tightens rules for anonymous cash deposits
item.description: The National Bank of Kyrgyzstan is proposing changes to tighten rules for anonymous cash deposits into bank accounts, cards, and e-wallets via payment terminals. The new regulations would require user identification for such transactions, excluding low-risk payments like utilities and taxes.

item.title: Eurasian Economic Union Launches Traceability Mechanism for Foreign Goods
item.description: Starting September 1, 2026, the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) implemented a traceability mechanism for foreign goods cleared in one member state and moved to others. Initially, it covers refrigerators, washing machines, and televisions. The system aims to protect businesses from unfair competition and assure consumers of legal import.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Expand Meat Imports from India and Grow Jute on 50,000 Hectares
item.description: Uzbekistan and India intend to expand cooperation in agriculture and food. Uzbekistan is interested in increasing meat imports from India and is testing new salt-tolerant cotton varieties. Joint ventures are being established for meat production, with significant plans for the coming years.

item.title: Tajikistan faces mudslide threat in mountain regions September 3-4
item.description: Tajikistan's Agency for Hydrometeorology warns of mudslides in mountainous areas of republican subordination, Sughd region, and western Gorno-Badakhshan from September 3-4. Authorities advise residents to avoid livestock grazing, wood gathering, fishing, and hunting, and tour companies to cancel mountain hikes.

item.title: Uzbekistan President holds dialogue on improving business conditions
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with entrepreneurs in Khiva to discuss improving conditions for businesses. The focus shifted from supporting startups to fostering growth for existing enterprises, emphasizing access to finance, technology, markets, and a predictable regulatory environment. Business credit portfolios have nearly tripled.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Organize Free Extracurricular Classes for Children from Poor Families
item.description: Uzbekistan will establish free extracurricular clubs in schools, technical schools, and educational centers for children from low-income families. This initiative aims to address the lack of specific programs for engaging impoverished youth in vocational training. Youth leaders, district governor's assistants, and women's activists will be tasked with organizing these clubs.

item.title: Two Individuals Apprehended Attempting to Smuggle $240,000 Out of Uzbekistan
item.description: Customs officials at the "Navoi" border post in Tashkent region intercepted two individuals attempting to smuggle $240,000 out of Uzbekistan. One woman was found with $80,000 and the other with $160,000, concealed and strapped to their legs under clothing. The State Customs Committee reported the incident and released video footage.

item.title: Crimean Tatar Athletes Representing Ukraine Received Applause in Bishkek
item.description: Refat Chubarov, head of the Crimean Tatar National Assembly, stated that Crimean Tatar athletes representing Ukraine at the opening ceremony of the VI World Nomad Games in Bishkek were met with applause. He noted that the Ukrainian delegation, though small, received enthusiastic reception. Leaders from various countries attended the event.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Revise Criteria for Providing Credits and Subsidies, Empowering Governor's Assistants
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to change the criteria for granting credits, subsidies, and compensations, moving away from fixed decrees. The Ministry of Economy and Central Bank will update financing mechanisms quarterly based on regional potential. 8,992 district governor's assistants will be evaluated, with top performers receiving promotions and bonuses, and underperformers replaced.

item.title: Uzbekistan to revise social registry for targeted poverty reduction and expanded support
item.description: Uzbekistan will change its approach to identifying needy families and expand social support measures, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced. The national social protection agency will review the social registry system by year-end. The evaluation will shift to a multidimensional approach, considering chronic illnesses, disability, multiple children, and family members working abroad. Working mothers will receive benefits until their child turns one.

item.title: Four Uzbek citizens arrested in South Korea for allegedly financing Syrian terrorist group
item.description: Four Uzbek citizens have been arrested in South Korea on suspicion of financing terrorism. They are accused of providing financial support, including cryptocurrency and vehicles, to the "Katibah Tawhid wal Jihod" group operating in Syria. Investigations revealed one suspect purchased 11 used cars and two excavators for the group.

item.title: Uzbekistan to implement new poverty reduction and employment system
item.description: Uzbekistan will introduce a new system for poverty reduction and employment enhancement, announced President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. Regional and district poverty reduction headquarters will receive additional powers and resources totaling 3.2 trillion Uzbek soums. Local leaders will dedicate three days weekly to poverty and employment issues.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Implement New System for Poverty Reduction and Income Growth
item.description: Uzbekistan will introduce a completely new system to combat poverty and increase incomes, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced. Districts will receive 3.2 trillion soums, and local authorities will focus solely on poverty and employment issues three days a week. This approach was developed after analyzing poverty reduction strategies in Khorezm region.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Faces Climate Crisis as Glaciers Melt, Causing Billions in Damage
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is confronting a climate crisis with rapidly melting glaciers, leading to significant damage. Temperatures are rising, glacier coverage has decreased by 16-17% since 2000, and glacial lake outburst floods pose increasing risks. The government is developing a National Adaptation Plan to manage climate risks.

item.title: Bobojon Ghafurov's book "Tajiks" published in German
item.description: To mark the 35th anniversary of Tajikistan's independence, Bobojon Ghafurov's seminal work "Tajiks" has been translated and published in German. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs reports this initiative aims to popularize the ancient culture of the Tajik people. International scholars praised the translation's timeliness and significance.

item.title: Uzbekistan Engages in High-Level Diplomatic Meetings with India, Azerbaijan, and Pakistan
item.description: Uzbekistan's foreign policy prioritizes trust and cooperation. Prime Minister Modi visited Uzbekistan for talks with President Mirziyoyev on August 29-30, focusing on trade, energy, and healthcare. Meetings also occurred between Azerbaijan and Armenia, and Uzbekistan and Pakistan, discussing economic and regional issues.
